questions.title: How do you address a Collection and a single Entry in an OData V2 resource path (Collection, KeyPredicate)?
questions.description: To address entries you start with a Collection: the name of an entity set, or of a service operation that returns a collection of entries. Following it with a KeyPredicate selects a single entry. The KeyPredicate is written in parentheses: if the entry has a single key property, it may contain only the key value, as in Categories(1); if the key consists of two or more properties, the values must be given as comma-separated name=value pairs. The canonical URI of an entry is the service root plus one segment made of the collection name and the key predicate, for example Products(1), even though the same entry might also be reachable through a longer path such as Categories(1)/Products(1). A collection may also be followed by /$count to address the number of its entries.
keyPoints: Collection = entity set name (or a service operation returning entries).
KeyPredicate = key value(s) in parentheses: Categories(1).
Composite key: name=value pairs separated by commas.
Canonical entry URI: serviceRoot/Collection(key).
Collection/$count addresses the number of entries.

examples.title: Addressing collections and entries
examples.code:
GET https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/Categories          all Categories (entity set "Categories")
GET https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/Categories(1)       the Category with key 1
GET https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/Products/$count     number of Products (returns 9)

Composite key (two key properties):
GET /Service.svc/OrderItems(OrderID=10248,ItemNo=1)

versionDiff.v2: Only as the last segment of a collection path: Products/$count.
versionDiff.v4: Also inside $filter and $orderby: Categories?$filter=Products/$count gt 2, Categories?$orderby=Products/$count.

versionDiff.v2: Every segment carries its full key.
versionDiff.v4: Key properties fixed by a referential constraint aren't repeated: ~/Orders(1)/Items(2).

questions.title: How do NavPropSingle and NavPropCollection segments work in a resource path?
questions.description: After a key predicate you can follow navigation properties to related entries. A NavPropSingle segment is the name of a navigation property of the entry from the prior segment that has a "to 1" relationship, so it identifies a single entry, for example Products(1)/Supplier. A NavPropCollection segment is the same, but the navigation property has a "to many" relationship, so it identifies a collection of entries, for example Categories(1)/Products. Because a NavPropCollection yields a collection, it can again be followed by a key predicate or by /$count, and segments can be chained, as in Categories(1)/Products(1)/Supplier. Each segment is described in the metadata by the navigation property of the same name on the corresponding entity type.
keyPoints: NavPropSingle: "to 1" navigation property; result is one entry.
NavPropCollection: "to many" navigation property; result is a collection.
A collection result can take a key predicate or /$count next.
Segments chain: Categories(1)/Products(1)/Supplier.

examples.title: Navigation in the V2 demo service
examples.code:
GET https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/Categories(1)/Products              Products of Category 1 (NavPropCollection)
GET https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/Categories(1)/Products/$count       how many of them
GET https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/Categories(1)/Products(1)/Supplier  the Supplier of that Product (NavPropSingle)

versionDiff.v2: Defined by an Association and the AssociationSet that binds it to entity sets.
versionDiff.v4: Navigation properties are unidirectional; an optional NavigationPropertyBinding names the target entity set.

questions.title: How do you address a property, a complex-type property and a raw value in a resource path?
questions.description: To address a property, you append the property name to the path of the entry. A Property segment is the name of a declared or dynamic property of the entry or complex type from the prior segment, for example Categories(1)/Name. If the property is of a complex type, a ComplexType segment addresses the whole structured value, for example Suppliers(1)/Address, and a further Property segment addresses one field inside it, for example .../Supplier/Address/City. Adding /$value to a primitive property addresses its raw value instead of its OData-formatted representation, for example .../Address/City/$value returns just Sammamish as plain text. In the metadata, these segments are described by the properties of the entity type or the complex type.
keyPoints: Property segment: Categories(1)/Name.
ComplexType segment: Suppliers(1)/Address (the whole complex value).
Property inside a complex type: .../Address/City.
/$value: the raw value of a primitive property.

examples.title: Property paths in the V2 demo service

versionDiff.v2: Raw value of a primitive property.
versionDiff.v4: Raw value of a primitive or enumeration property, for example People('russellwhyte')/Gender/$value on TripPin.

versionDiff.v2: Complex types have only structural properties.
versionDiff.v4: Complex types can also have navigation properties, so a path can continue from a complex property to related entities.

questions.title: How are service operations (function imports) addressed in a URI?
questions.description: A service operation is addressed like a resource: the service root URI followed by the name of the operation, optionally followed by a question mark and its parameters as ParamName=ParamValue pairs. Parameter values use the URI literal forms of the primitive types, so a string is written in single quotes. The order of parameters does not matter, and query string parameters that the operation does not define are ignored for the invocation. If the operation returns a collection of entries and the service author enables query composition, it acts as a pseudo collection: further path segments such as a key predicate or a navigation property can follow it. The spec shows this with ProductsByColor(3)/Category/Name?color='red'; the V2 demo service does not enable it, so there GetProductsByRating(1)/Category returns 404. An operation without parameters is addressed by its name only, as in the spec example ProductColors.
keyPoints: serviceRoot/OperationName?param1=value1&param2=value2.
Values use URI literal forms (strings in single quotes).
Parameter order is insignificant; undefined parameters are ignored.
More path segments after the operation only if the service enables composition.

examples.title: Calling the real operation of the V2 demo service
examples.code:
GET https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/GetProductsByRating?rating=5
GET https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/GetProductsByRating?rating=5&param=foo     (param is not defined: ignored)

versionDiff.v2: Service operations, invoked with GET or POST as m:HttpMethod says.
versionDiff.v4: Functions (no side effects, may be composed further) and actions (side effects, invoked with POST, not composable).
Function parameters as plain query options were pruned; the call names @ parameter aliases whose values follow in the query: Products/Model.WithIngredients(Ingredients=@i)?@i=["Carrots"].

questions.title: How do you address the links between entries with $links in OData V2?
questions.description: OData treats relationships as first-class constructs, so associations between entries can be addressed just like the entries themselves. The URI is the URI of a single entry, followed by /$links/ and the name of a navigation property declared on that entry. Categories(1)/$links/Products identifies the set of links to the products related to Category 1, and Products(1)/$links/Category identifies the link to the category of Product 1. Compared with Categories(1)/Products, which returns the related entries themselves, the $links URI returns only references (URIs) to them. The link resources are what you use to change relationships directly. A POST to a $links URI adds a link, with the URI of the target entry in the body. A PUT to a single-valued link, such as Products(1)/$links/Category, replaces it, again with the new URI in the body. A DELETE on a URI that names one link, such as Categories(1)/$links/Products(10), removes it and has no body. In OData V4 the $links segment was replaced by /$ref.
keyPoints: Syntax: Entry URI + /$links/ + NavigationProperty.
Returns link references (URIs), not the related entries.
POST adds a link and PUT replaces one (new URI in the body); DELETE removes one (no body).
Replaced by /$ref in OData V4.

examples.title: Reading and changing links in the V2 demo service
examples.code:
GET    https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/Categories(1)/$links/Products
GET    https://services.odata.org/V2/OData/OData.svc/Products(1)/$links/Category

POST   /V2/OData/OData.svc/Categories(1)/$links/Products     body: <uri>.../Products(10)</uri>
PUT    /V2/OData/OData.svc/Products(1)/$links/Category       body: <uri>.../Categories(2)</uri>
DELETE /V2/OData/OData.svc/Categories(1)/$links/Products(10)  (no body)

versionDiff.v4: /$links/ was pruned; append /$ref to a path instead: Categories(1)/Products/$ref.
~/$entity?$id=<entity-id> returns the current representation of the referenced entity.
